title: Event
description: One line of a benchmark's stdout. A benchmark prints a stream of these, one JSON object per line, and nothing else on stdout. The six universal events below have exactly the fields listed. A benchmark may also emit events of its own, under any other name, with any fields beside `event` and `t`. A schema of one line cannot hold the stream's order, which is a rule of its own: started first and once, and in a stream that is recorded without quick: true; finished last and once; samples numbered from 0 in order, each starting only when none is open and at a t no earlier than the previous sample's sample_ended; every sample_ended closing the open sample, of the same number, at a t no earlier than its start, and every sample closed; each observed key once; exactly one verified; and at least one sample whose warmup is false.

event.description: The event's name: one of the six universal events, started, observed, sample_started, sample_ended, verified and finished, whose fields are fixed; or a benchmark's own, under any other name.

t.description: Whole nanoseconds on the clock that `started` names.

schema.description: Which version of the stream's shape the binary prints.

wall_utc.description: The wall clock read straight after `t`, to the nanosecond.

clock.description: The clock every `t` is read from.

clock_read_ns.description: The median cost of one clock read, measured at startup.

quick.description: True for a developer's trial stream, from the binary's quick mode, which is never recorded.

then.description: What the program observed about its own work. May appear more than once; each key appears once across all of them.

values.description: What the benchmark observed of its own work, by key: the counterparts of its parameters, as it documents them, never a value it was told. bytes_per_repetition, when it is among them, is what bytes per second are derived from.

then.description: The start edge of one sample. Samples are numbered from 0 and never overlap.

sample.description: The sample's number: from 0, in stream order.

warmup.description: True for a warmup sample: printed and tagged, never dropped, and never counted.

repetitions.description: How many repetitions of the measured work lie between the sample's two edges, 1 or more.

then.description: The end edge of the sample with the same number.

sample.description: The number of the sample it closes: the open one.

then.description: A value derived from the data the measured work processed.

checksum.description: The value, 0x and sixteen lower-case hex digits: derived from the data the measured work processed, so that a compiler cannot delete the work.

then.description: Always last. Its absence is evidence of a crash.
